definition: Self-talk is a psychological intervention in which a person uses their own internal or spoken statements to help support coping. In the supplied source, it is described as a commonly used method for athletes aiming to manage demands related to performance.

reasons: The packet supports self-talk as a commonly used psychological intervention to support coping, but it does not support the added explanation that it involves a person using their own internal or spoken statements.

The claim that it is used by athletes to manage demands related to performance goes beyond the packet, which only says it is a commonly used psychological intervention for athletes aiming to achieve peak performance and support coping.
The definition is not fully supported as written by the supplied source packet.

The definition states that self-talk involves “internal or spoken statements,” but the supplied packet only says self-talk is a psychological intervention and does not describe its content (e.g., internal vs. spoken).
